utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, case number IT-01-47-T, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Can we have the appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours, Counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Mathias Neuner, Daryl Mundis, and our case manager, Andres Vatter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Mundis. And the appearances for the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours. On behalf of General Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, lead counsel; and Stephane Bourgon, co-counsel. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura, Rodney Dixon, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and Nermin Mulalic, legal assistant. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Chamber bids good afternoon to all those present on this Monday afternoon, representatives of the Prosecution, the Defence counsel, the accused, as well as all the staff members of this courtroom. As we indicated last week, this day should be devoted to the continuation of the screening of the videotapes, and the Chamber also planned next Wednesday another hearing when we can deal with outstanding issues. But if today we manage to view all the remaining videos and if we have a chance to address the matters that we had planned for Wednesday, in that case we would not have to have another hearing on Wednesday. But we need to have information from the Prosecution: first, the approximate time and duration of the videos that are going to be shown; and secondly, have you had any reaction from Mrs. Benjamin, who went on site regarding the archivists? So, Mr. Withopf [as interpreted], can you tell us where we stand, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'll leave the issue of the videos and the length of the videos to my colleague, Mr. Neuner. With respect to Ms. Benjamin and her mission last week to Sarajevo, she has in fact returned to The Hague; however, she phoned me this morning and she returned to The Hague with some kind of illness and she is not in the office today. So I have not had a full opportunity to discuss issues with her. Again, based on discussions that I had with her on Friday, however, I do not anticipate that we will have a problem filling the week of the 21st of June with witnesses. However, as of this moment, I do not have the specific names nor do I have the witness statements in a format to be disclosed to the Defence. I anticipate being able to disclose witness statements to the Defence tomorrow, again assuming that Ms. Benjamin makes a full and speedy recovery and is in the office tomorrow. Again, Mr. President, with respect to the videos, I turn to my colleague Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Mundis. Mr. Neuner, you have the floor to present the videotapes, and more specifically, could you tell us the total duration that you envisage that the tapes will take.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, Defence counsel, and everybody in and around the courtroom. I have prepared an order list for Your Honours and the parties. Let me ask the usher to distribute this. On this list are 11 excerpts and the total length of these excerpts is 96 minutes. The overwhelming majority of these excerpts come from the reserve list. The Prosecution has also made efforts and revisited some of the tapes from which excerpts have been shown already last week, and as Your Honours can see, about 50 per cent of these excerpts here have a short duration, and there are a few excerpts which have a longer duration. I just learnt a moment ago from one of the Defence counsels that the tapes on order 6 till 10, which is basically one in the same tape, 2414, that -- V000-2414, that there is uncertainty whether the Defence has fully received that tape in the process of the disclosure. My understanding is that the tape carrying this ERN number has been disclosed but that the content -- it's unclear whether the content matches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand you well, we still have 11 clips to view which you numbered from 1 to 11. The duration of each tape is clearly indicated: 1 minute; 1 minute; then 2 minutes for the third; the fourth, 3 minutes; the fifth, 4 minutes; the sixth, which will be the longest, 42 minutes; the seventh 9 minutes; the ninth 16 minutes; the tenth 5 minutes; and the 11th, 1 minute approximately. So in total about one and a half hours of videotapes. So we have plenty of time to view all the videos on this list. The Defence appears to have a problem regarding the video with the number 2414, because on that video there are several parts corresponding to 6, 7, 8, 9, and 10, and the Defence is not quite sure that it was disclosed to them. The Prosecution tells us that they did disclose these documents to them. So what can the Defence tell us regarding this problem, the Prosecution having told us that Defence counsel did receive in time the mentioned videotapes? However, even if you didn't receive them, the binder containing the transcripts allowed you to familiarise yourselves with those tapes and the contents of the tapes, because tape 2414 appears under number 7 -- as tab number 7 of the mentioned binder. As I have V000-2414, tab 7. The transcript is in English and in B/C/S. Does the Defence wish to make any comments regarding this document 2414? Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Madam Judge and Your Honours. I simply wish to remind the Chamber that last week we were having arguments regarding the last tape viewed and we would like to present our arguments regarding that video. As for the other videotapes, my colleague from the Kubura Defence will speak on behalf of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the best thing would be to first give the floor to Mr. Dixon to hear their opinion regarding 2414, and afterwards I will give you the floor, Mr. Bourgon, for your observations. Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Good afternoon, Your Honours. In respect of the video 2414, I've been advised that this was a video that was only -- we were only notified this morning was going to be shown today in the court. It was disclosed to us earlier, but when we checked the CD-ROM that it was disclosed on, that number appears on the CD-ROM, but the material is in fact not recorded on the CD-ROM. So we have the transcript but we do not have the images on the CD-ROM, and that's what we require in order to be able to review this video before it is shown in court to Your Honours. To it appears to be a technical problem. It is on the transcript clear that it is meant to be some image of alleged destruction in the Kakanj area, which is, as a side issue, not a charge made in the indictment but nevertheless from the transcript we can deduce that. But Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. when we look at the CD-ROM, we can't see those images and would require those to be disclosed to us before they are shown to Your Honours. Perhaps that can be done in the break, with the assistance of my learned friends from the Prosecution. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is precisely what I thought and that is, since you are five lawyers, that the CD-ROM could be shown to you immediately and then after the break we can broadcast the tape 2414. But as the break lasts 30 minutes, perhaps you won't have time to view everything, because tab 6 lasts 42 minutes. So it would be best for one of you to leave the courtroom to go and view the tape before it is broadcast in court. This could be a solution since you do have the transcript in your possession. Mr. Dixon, would it not be possible for one of you to go and view this CD-ROM before the break -- as of now, including the break time? Because the break is 30 minutes, whereas the tape will last at least 42 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We can view this tape on our own computer which is in the courtroom, so we don't have to leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bourgon, you have the floor. We are listening.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, when we left last week, we had just viewed a videotape concerning destruction of houses and other facilities in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The Chamber noted following the viewing that these were scenes of devastation, and they appeared to be at the beginning of the winter and the villages we saw were in a very dramatic case, in a dramatic condition. But I think -- we think that it is not admissible. We will divide the arguments into two parts: first of all, the commentary that accompanies the video; and secondly, the question of the actual images. Contrary to my custom, I will begin with the commentary. The person commenting this videotape is a person that has already been heard in this Chamber at the beginning of the trial. This witness, when testifying in the chamber, was not shown this video and no questions were put to her about that video and we were not in a position to cross-examine that witness regarding the contents of that tape. The testimony of that witness in the courtroom differs considerably from what appears to be her commentary on the videotape, so this is actually a second testimony. And unless the witness is brought back to the chamber for us to be able to cross-examine her, then the commentary itself should be declared inadmissible for this trial. I pass on now to the second question; that is, the question of the pictures, the images. These images date back to 1997. We don't know exactly when the houses that we saw were destroyed -- when they were destroyed. We don't know who destroyed those houses, and we don't know how those houses were destroyed. Nevertheless, we do know on the basis of the evidence heard during this trial that this was a regular scene following attacks. During the days and weeks that followed, there was destruction after an attack, destruction committed by civilians and all kinds of people, be they criminals or simply refugees. Clearly, Mr. President, this videotape from 1997 can give an impression of destruction and devastation, an impression of totally razed villages. However, we feel that that impression should not be admitted as evidence in this trial, because, first of all, the pictures that we saw were not relevant -- are not relevant, as we do not have any link between the destruction and the charges against the accused in this trial because, as I was saying a moment ago, we don't know who, when, or how the destruction was committed. Therefore, to take destruction in these -- Bosnia in 1997 as evidence would be very dangerous for this case. We refer to Rule 89(D) which we feel can be fully applied in this case; that is, evidence admitted as such can have -- be more prejudicial with respect to its probative value. So the probative value of this evidence is so minimal, that is, significantly exceeded by the interests of a fair trial [as interpreted]. So first of all, the commentary, and also the pictures, the two parts of this video that we viewed last week should be declared inadmissible. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Bourgon. I will give the floor to the Prosecution, who, if they wish, can respond to the two arguments set forth by the Defence, regarding the commentary and the images. Regarding the commentary, the Defence tells us that the person commenting on those -- commenting those images could have been cross-examined if she had been present during the viewing, which would have allowed the Defence to ask her questions about the tape. And that is why the Defence is requesting that the commentary of this videotape should not be admitted. The second point has to do with the images. The Defence makes three basic observations: Who, when, and how. The Defence is of the opinion that we don't know who carried out the destruction; the question of when, we don't know, as the videotape was filmed in 1997, whereas the events covered by the indictment date back to 1993. And also we do not know how the destruction was carried out. The Defence is of the opinion that there are three possibilities: Either it may have been done by civilians, or by criminals, or perhaps refugees. For all these reasons the Defence submits that this video is inadmissible as a whole. And finally, the Defence refers to 89(D), and that is there has to be a balance between the rights of the accused and a fair trial and the probative value of the evidence, which in their opinion is considerably below the level required not to effect a fair trial, the fairness of the trial [as interpreted]. And that is why the Defence would submit that the Chamber should not admit this videotape into evidence. Can the Prosecution respond to these observations, which we are not hearing for the first time. Surely Mr. Dixon will be speaking along the same lines, and you have the floor, Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honours. I do wish to make a few points in support of the submissions made by Mr. Bourgon. Our point of view is also that the video should not be admitted into evidence. The timing of when the destruction occurred is, of course, extremely pertinent in this case, as Your Honours may be aware from the cross-examination of certain witnesses. In relation to the alleged destruction in the Ovnak and Strmac area, the Defence of Mr. Kubura is that the 7th Brigade left that area shortly after the attack which was completed on 8 June, certainly by 10 June. And hence the time when any alleged destruction did take place is critical for any charges that are laid against Mr. Kubura, as the commander of the 7th Brigade. These images were taken many years later, and it's impossible from viewing the images to say when any of the destruction that one might see on the video did occur, and certainly not possible to say if it occurred on the 10th, 11th, or 12th of June, which, from the Defence point of view, is the critical question for Your Honours to decide in relation to this charge. Your Honours, in addition to that, there are significant distinctions between what the witness said in his testimony, where he wasn't as clear about what destruction did occur. This is Witness ZM, who testified on the 19th of March of this year and the comments that he did make on the tape. There are some points that are similar; for example, he indicates that there was no destruction in the Brajkovici village. But there are many points that differ, and for those reasons alone we say that the video is unreliable and Your Honours should turn to what he said before Your Honours in the witness box, when there was an Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. opportunity to put the videotape to him and to confirm whether his commentary on that tape was correct or not. Your Honours, just on the commentary, there's another point. Although we were not experts in sound, but when looking at the images it appears that the commentary was recorded after the images were recorded. The sounds that are in the background when the commentary is being made do not appear to be sounds that would normally come across when driving in a vehicle and filming. It appears that it was done much later. That might be a question that we cannot finally determine because we don't have expertise, but another point going to the reliability, we say, of this evidence. Finally, Your Honours, there was mention made in the commentary about the 7th Brigade sign or words being visible on a particular house. We've looked again and again at the images, and even though that's in the commentary, that doesn't appear to be what the images show. It's certainly unclear what is on a particular house. And that would be another reason for excluding is commentary and those images. Your Honour, for all of those reasons, we would request that this videotape be excluded from the evidence in this case. I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Dixon. I shall give the floor now to the Prosecution. I don't know whether it's going to be Mr. Neuner or Mr. Mundis who's going to respond. But I think can speak on behalf of the other two Judges as well. One may wonder why this videotape, and on a more general level other evidence, why the Prosecution did not choose to show them when the witness was present. If that had been done, we wouldn't be having this debate. The Prosecution is not obliged to answer this particular question that I'm putting to them as -- on my own behalf, but the question that the Judges may wonder is why it was not broadcast when the witness was present. So, Mr. Mundis, can you give us an answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, as the Trial Chamber may be aware, a number of attorneys have appeared for the Prosecution in this case. As a general rule, the attorney taking the witness is responsible for which exhibits or videotapes are to be shown or produced through that witness. I am attempting to via e-mail find an answer to that question. The attorney who took this witness is still employed with the Office of the Prosecutor but is no longer assigned to this case. As I've said, I've sent an e-mail to him in an attempt to find out precisely why that was not the case, and I might respectfully suggest that we perhaps could return to that specific issue at a later time, if it's appropriate to do so. I simply don't have an answer is the bottom line, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you for your answer. You have more or less answered the question I put to you a while ago. So we have noted at this stage of the proceedings what the Defence counsels have told us, and the Chamber at any rate will have to render a decision on this. That said, we can now continue the proceedings, and I would like to turn now to Mr. Neuner and ask him to show us the first videotape, which is about to be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the first videotape on your list is V000-1440. This is a video sequence from the TV news dealing with the Mujahedin presence in Bosnia-Herzegovina. The Vahabi sect is mentioned. The producer was Studio B, which reads, Information provided by a correspondent from the British newspaper the Daily Telegraph. The Prosecution has tried to give a date -- to attach this particular news to a date and the date is in September 1992, so prior to the indictment period. This is an inference drawn from the fact that the videotape itself contained numerous news excerpts in sort of chronological order and the Prosecution has just looked at the previous and the following sequences and tried to, draw an inference from there. So the Prosecution believes it's September 1992. It's a one-minute sequence from Studio B or NTV, which is Independent TV in Belgrade. And the source who has provided this video news compilation to the ICTY was Natasha Kandic, who is executive director of the Humanitarian Law Fund. I believe, for the translators, a rough translation can be found in tab number 21 of the binder, and the relevant excerpt is from 1 hour 24 minutes running for about 1 minute, and the excerpt will be shown now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] This is an attack of Muslims on a convoy. Karadzic's letter was published in London. Karadzic warns that Serbs will not be carrying out defence, that they will be forced to occupy all the territories that they had left. "I'm afraid that only days separate us from a catastrophe," says Karadzic in his letter. The report of the Daily Telegraph from Zagreb says that in Bosnia there are no Mujahedins and we read in this report that Mujahedins were seen in Travnik and that they are not Arabic students. In his --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a videotape which lasts one minute. In the beginning we see a picture of Karadzic; and then two speakers, a man and a woman, part of a television crew from Belgrade. And they talk about this letter from Karadzic that mentions the Mujahedin and these Mujahedin would be part of -- or would belong to an extremist sect called Vahabi. So that's all we can infer from this excerpt. I shall now give the floor to the Defence team. Does the Defence team have any comments to make? The Trial Chamber would like to hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. This is a videotape. It is said that this videotape goes back to September 1992. We don't know anything about that. Once again, we don't know who prepared this report. Is it something which was collated afterwards? We just don't know. Whatever the case may be, on viewing this video it seems like this is an excerpt from the news bulletin for Belgrade station providing news on Zagreb. I think the reliability of such a tape can be questioned. When we look at the content of this videotape, this videotape provides no new piece of information. The fact that there might have been Mujahedin there, if the date were 100 per cent correct, then of course it might be relevant. But in this particular case, as the information is not particularly reliable, we don't know at what time the Mujahedin were actually in Travnik. This is a question which has come up again and again in the course of this trial, and this video would only confuse the evidentiary material even more than has been the case before. So once again, we would like this videotape -- this exhibit not to be admitted. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Dixon, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, nothing further to add to what Mr. Bourgon has said, Your Honours, except to say that the translation at tab 21 that we have does not correspond to what we've just seen on our screens. The translation we have at tab 21 is a report from Ankara, Turkey and lasts some two and a half pages. So we don't have any transcript at tab 21 for what we've seen. Perhaps it's elsewhere and the Prosecution could direct us to where it is. But nothing further to add, other than that. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Dixon, if you turn to page 3, you would have found it there. On page 3, at the bottom of the page, you can read: "Studio B."

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: I'm grateful, Your Honours. In other words, only that portion was shown and not any of the previous sections. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The last question raises an issue as far as we are concerned. In Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. our view -- in other words, we would like the video excerpts, which will be viewed before the Trial Chamber, as well as the excerpts we have in the binder. We understand full well, Your Honour, that only those excerpts from the videotapes which we would like to see admitted are excerpts which we can actually view before the Trial Chamber. And the reports which are not part of those excerpts viewed before the Trial Chamber, be not admitted into evidence. I just wanted to make this clear that there can be no confusion about this, that the video excerpts can be admitted but the reports that go along with these video excerpts should not be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Let me turn to the Prosecution. At tab number 21, we can see that several reports are included here and these reports probably refer to other video excerpts. You have selected the Studio B excerpt only, the one that's right at the end, which means that all the other reports can -- could not be admitted into evidence because they have not been presented. Let me give the floor back to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, as the Defence has rightly pointed out, it is not the Prosecution's intention to tender anything else than the excerpt shown in open court -- to tender anything else into evidence or ask for its admission into evidence. The binder was simply prepared to give, especially the Defence, notice about other sections of this tape, because the Prosecution believes it's in the interests of -- to find out the truth that also the other party has certain excerpts of transcripts of translations of certain excerpts available. With regard to this particular tape, my understanding of having looked into the information index form, the so-called IF form, this tape forms part of a larger collection which can be -- which is internally be called the Red Tape Collection, which means nothing else than that on the so-called red tapes simply video footage from news sessions on TV Belgrade have been recorded in more or less chronological order. What I can see here from the IF in front of me is that, for example, the first tape starts on -- the first excerpt starts on 3 September 1992 - that's what the IF indicates to me - and the last sequence, for example, on this tape dates from 26 April 1993. And in between there are, yeah, some excerpts containing news always on TV Belgrade. Whether these were evening news, morning news, I cannot tell. However, having looked also at other collections or other tapes of this collection, the tapes, the so-called red tapes, yeah, they follow a kind of chronological order. This excerpt has been selected just to demonstrate that at an early point in time, in 1992 in September, the issue of Mujahedin has been discussed not only on the side of the Bosnian Muslims, but rather also on the side of the adversaries to the conflict. The Prosecution is well aware that this small excerpt just reflects the view of one side of the conflict, and to be precise, Radovan Karadzic is mentioned here. It just reflects what in the news at a particular place in Belgrade is reported about the Mujahedin. And the Prosecution is simply of the opinion that the tape only demonstrates that the issue of Mujahedin was not only discussed in Central Bosnia as such but had a kind of -- was in the public arena and was discussed also by the other sides.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Would you like to show the next video now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, all these videos - just one more announcement - are drawn from the so-called reserve list, so the Prosecution is well aware that, like the previous video, they do not necessarily relate directly to crimes committed in the indictment but can be also of a more peripheral nature, meaning that they describe climate of discussion going on about events which are coming from Central Bosnia, namely the 3rd Corps area. And the next tape is V000-1729. A transcript and translation should be in tab 22 of the binder. And the sequence shown is 1 minute long. It's a juxtaposition taken from a movie or a video which is called "In Broad Daylight." The director is Ljubo Lasic. And the production was the GRAL film and Lakehurst Productions International, which is a film about war crimes committed in the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina. This tape has been broadcasted on Croatian TV on the 17th of February, 1999. The tape has been hand over by Mr. Amir Ahmic, the BiH liaison officer with the ICTY, and it has been handed over to Mr. John Ralston, former staff member, former chief of investigations in the Office of the Prosecutor. The sequence selected relates to expert opinions shown on the influence of radical Islamic groups on -- the influence which these -- the presence of radical Islamic groups had on the population of Bosnia. We will hear a statement from Mr. Daniel Nelson, and the Prosecution has made further inquiries about the personality of Mr. Daniel Nelson. Mr. Daniel Nelson, I cite here, has a Ph.D. from the Johns Hopkins University and he became Dean of Arts and Science at the University of New Haven in August 2002, in the United States. From January 1999 onwards he served as a professor of Civil-Military Relations at the George C. Marshall Center for European Security Studies in Garmisch in Germany from 2000 to 2002. He was at some point in time US State Department official. And just one more information -- yeah. He was also an observer of the Balkan Arms Trafficking from 1992 up to 1994. And while he was working at the US State Department, he was working there in the Kosovo section. So the excerpt, being very brief, just one minute, will be screened now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Could you tell us which page on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I have here on my footage, the relevant footage, 18 minutes 50 seconds till 20 minutes. And this is page 7.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] When the Serbs withdrew to 35 kilometres --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just to identify Mr. Nelson, because here the transcript page 7 gives just "male voice." It's the second male voice starting at 18.52, and the relevant excerpts selected starts at 18.50. So a few seconds earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: THE NARRATOR: ... Mujahedin of various kinds that came into the country and began to spread more of the fundamentalist idea. Even the population of Sarajevo and also the nature of the government have become more Islamic over time. So I think it's fair to say that as a consequence of the war, that -- yet the suffering was enormous among the Muslim population, and we need to bear that in mind -- but one negative consequence of the war, certainly, has been increasing radicalisation of the Muslim population and that's probably not -- not a good sign, because it does not help Bosnia to integrate itself within Europe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So this excerpt, which lasts 1 minute, we can hear the commentary and we see images of soldiers who are wearing a military uniform, who are shouting in Arabic. And we even see a flag, a green flag, which someone is waving. In the background, we can recognise a landscape which we've seen in other videos prior to this one. This is what we're able to see, rather quickly. The Defence team, what would you like to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would first and foremost like to make a comment or, rather, draw the attention of the Trial Chamber on the following, something which has been the case since the beginning of this video footage, something we've mentioned several times already. My colleague from the Prosecution talks about internal systems which would bear the name of IF. If the Trial Chamber is to view a tape in the presence of a witness who could recognise the contents of this same video, this would mean that we would not have to understand the date of production of this video because the witness himself could then provide this information. In the absence of any witness who could identify or authenticate this video, it is therefore crucial to understand how the video was actually prepared, how the video landed in the hands of the Prosecution, and how this video was selected. Just to give you an example: In the last excerpt we talked about red tape, which according to the Prosecution would be a series of news bulletins between various dates. Your Honour, we feel, therefore, that the Prosecution cannot provide evidence material as such and it is too soon to provide submissions, and how the Trial Chamber can infer anything by viewing this video footage. So the Prosecution tells us, as regards the last video excerpt that it wanted to show us, that the question of the Mujahedin was something which extended beyond Bosnia and Herzegovina. We feel that this argument has nothing to do with this excerpt, it has to do with the intention of the Prosecution. So we feel that these submissions should only be mentioned when it comes to adducing the evidence in this case. At the moment we are only talking about a stage when exhibits will be adduced into evidence. The Prosecution is presenting its material, but we feel that the submissions should be made at a latter stage. Now, as far as this excerpt is concerned, there is no direct connection with the crimes alleged in the indictment, and these are peripheral to the indictment, as was mentioned, so I think that in this case the Prosecution admits that this video is by and large not relevant. In addition, as far as the making of this video is concerned, we have the name of a company, even if we know that this information does not come from any statement but comes from the Prosecution. We have a viewing date, which is February 1999, and we have the date alongside the name of the author. We don't have the date of the footage; we don't know when this videotape was actually broadcast. We know nothing about the Lakehurst International Productions either. Is this a production company, a propaganda production company? Is this any serious firm? We just don't know. We just know that a representative from the embassy would have probably got hold of this videotape after having viewed these excerpts in 1999 and handing them over to the investigators. Is it on the request of the Prosecution or did the embassy quite freely hand over these videotapes? Then comes the question of the commentator, Daniel Nelson. The Prosecution provides details of the CV of this gentlemen but we know nothing about him. We are told that he was a professor in 1992, that he worked in the United States at that date, but that he was in charge of Kosovo and he was an observer of the arms -- illegal dealing in Kosovo. Let me tell you, Your Honours, that we were all observers of illegal arms dealing in Kosovo at that time. The images that we have seen go back to what date? We don't know. These images were shot. We don't know at what time either. We see a green flag and we see signs in Arabic. We could, of course, connect this to the elements presented in the course of the trial, but I think it's much too easy to establish a connection between a green flag and Arabic inscriptions to infer that the scene we have seen is something which could play any role whatsoever in the evidence adduced in this case. And this might even be a prejudice for the accused, so that would go well and away beyond the evidence of this small video excerpt. If the Prosecution wanted to hear an expert on the question of Mujahedin, as they allege that this Mr. Daniel Nelson is an excerpt, why didn't they call him as a witness so that we would clearly get a fair understanding of this issue, rather than showing short excerpts to try and impress the Trial Chamber with the latter? We are -- the Trial Chamber cannot be influenced by such slim evidence. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. The main point is that the Prosecution should not be permitted to introduce expert opinion or analysis through a video like this. They have the opportunity to call experts for cross-examination. Even General Reinhardt may have been able to address some of these matters in his expert testimony. And then secondly, Your Honours, as Mr. Bourgon has pointed out, the images of the soldiers, the same three questions come up in relation to these images as have occurred in respect of many of the videos, which is who, when, and where. We don't have any answers to these questions. There's a flag, yes, but the witnesses who have come before, many of the international witnesses have indicated that these types of flags were used by many units in many areas. So in our submission, this short excerpt can be of no assistance to Your Honours and should not be admitted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. If the Prosecution wishes to respond or to introduce the next clip, whichever.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just briefly, Your Honours. The Prosecution in the course of the presentation of video sequences has put more and more effort on providing background information on the producer, on the tape, on the submitter, and now for one of the first times even on the speaker who appears on this tape. So the more and more information the Prosecution tries to assemble in order to satisfy the Defence in its request for more information, the more and more criticism is mentioned. The Prosecution, if Your Honours permit, will continue with providing background information which try to shed at least some light on what is being screened, to try to give some background information relating to the reliability Your Honours have to assess at some point in time. And insofar that this assists Your Honour, the Prosecution will continue in providing such information. Just briefly, what has been omitted by my learned colleagues of the Defence: On the two excerpts shown from the Mujahedin and throughout the statement provided -- or the brief commentary provided by Daniel Nelson, it could clearly be seen that Bosnian troops or Bosnian Mujahedin troops in 1993. So the date 1993, which is this -- which is identical to this indictment, was mentioned on the -- on both of the video footages shown about the Mujahedin. The Prosecution will now continue with the next sequence which relates to the same tape. And the following sequence is drawn from the timecode 26.15 till 27.58. This is basically page 9 following, on the English transcript or translation. And basically two persons give short commentaries here, both on Jihad. The first person is Imam Gadara, and it is displayed on the bottom of the tape, [B/C/S spoken] 1996, which can roughly be translated as "Pre-election rally of the ruling Bosnian party." Imam Gadara is giving the first short commentary, and the second is Imam Dzevad Hodzic, and also Daniel Nelson, who is already -- of whom we have already seen footage. Also Daniel Nelson gives a third statement. So it is from the same tape, and therefore the Prosecution does not repeat the information about the provider and submitter. The sequence will be shown now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] In the Islamic teaching, Jihad is our road. Jihad is our fight. Death on the Allah's road is our biggest honour. In the Islamic teaching, Jihad, the word and notion that is often used in different situations, in fact means to invest efforts to become serious; achieve a profit, a good goal. It further means that Jihad is equal to writing a good book and providing for one's family, working in a factory and building, reconstruction, and the defence of one's country. [In English] There were other Islamic forces within Bosnia, that were Bosniak themselves and did not come from the outside, that began to be stronger. And some parts of Izetbegovic's own party that were fundamentalist in nature began to be stronger and stronger all the time. What we do see in Bosnia is inroads and a more fundamentalist approach to religion, no question, because the Mujahedin were there; because the religion was under attack.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This video excerpt begins with Imam Gadara, who appears to be addressing an election rally and who said that "the Jihad is our struggle." "The Jihad is our struggle." After that, Mr. Daniel Nelson, whom we have already seen, explains that a part of the Bosniaks were a kind of fundamentalist element, and that is all that we can infer from this video excerpt, in which we saw an Imam speaking about the Jihad, followed by a commentator, who explains that among the Bosnians there were some who were certainly part of a fundamentalist movement. Please, Defence counsel, avoid repeating what you have already said.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Our comment regarding this video is the same as for the previous one, but I would like to add, Mr. President, two remarks: First, following what my learned friend from the Prosecution said, that they were endeavouring to provide more information, I don't know whether he said to satisfy or to give pleasure to the Defence. We would like to say that when the Prosecution provides more information, it is certainly not to please the Defence but to fulfil the burden that they have, the burden of proof. And we, too, will have the same burden when our case begins. So it is certainly not to please the Defence. It is a misinterpretation of our arguments regarding these videos. At the same time, Mr. President, we are looking at the small clips of film that are being shown and all we can see is that we are showing some kind of Mujahedin ghost in the background of this trial. We feel this is a discrimination against the language, the religion, the colour of a people, of a nation, and that has nothing to do with the trial we are concerned with. And I think that for this reason it is very important not to admit this evidence into -- this video into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... To add that this video clip, it's difficult to understand what relevance it could bring to the issues in this trial given that it was prepared, I understand, in 1996 and relates apparently to some political rally, but it's not clear at all which party's is the platform of the rally and whether that has any link to any of the political parties in 1993 or any of the imams who were present in 1993. And for that reason, beyond the Prosecution being able to give any more explanation as to the relevance of this particular clip to who were the persons and parties in 1993, our position is that it should not be admitted into evidence. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Prosecution now, if you wish to respond, or to introduce the next clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just very briefly. The relevance of this sequence is -- or this sequence is relating to paragraph 18 of the indictment, where the term "Jihad" or "holy war" in Bosnia is mentioned. And as Your Honours have pointed out, we have seen three opinions, and I just want to add this: The first imam which has been shown, Jamaal Gadara, I have here information. He was, in 1996 - so around the time when he was at this rally, and we could see the pre-election rally or the title of the pre-election rally and the year displayed on the video - he was the imam of the Islamic Studies Center. The second imam, who brought forward a more moderate view, was Dzevad Hodzic, or His Eminence Dzevad Hodzic, Grand Imam from the Zagreb Mosque. The Prosecution will now briefly summarise that the issue of Islamic fundamentalism, Jihad and so on, has been obviously discussed by experts such as Daniel Nelson, as well as inside the cleric or inside the religious leaders. And the next footage is taken from a tape which has already been shown last week. It's V000-3764, and just a short excerpt has been selected. It relates, again, to the gathering of the Battalion Jihad or El Mujahed Unit in Bosnia-Herzegovina in August 1993. This excerpt shows from this gathering, additional few seconds which basically hopefully will enlighten Your Honours with regard to the purpose of this gathering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And where can we find the transcript? On what page in the binder? The transcript of the tape, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It must be in tab 1. And I'm searching for the page. Your Honours, it is on page 29 of the transcript, of the English transcript. It says -- or it's in the big paragraph -- the second big paragraph, which starts with English voice-over: "The Mujahedin leadership," and it then continues.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: There is currently no audio. We'll make a second effort and try to fix this problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution asks whether we can already make now the technical break in order to arrange the audio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regarding the technical issue, when a sequence is being shown, can we make a still out of it? Can we stop the viewing for a moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, it's possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, when you play the tape, I would like you to stop when we see the person shooting with a pistol. It is now twenty-five to 4.00. We will resume around 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We shall now resume the hearing. And before giving the floor back to the Prosecution, I would like them to tell us more about these videos mentioned in the index which can be found in the binder. At five minutes past 4.00, we note that some videos are not listed, for instance, number 6, which matches 28.98; number 12, 26.29; 15, 24.00; 17, 28.95; 18, 16.76; and 20, 32.70 [as interpreted]. Does the Prosecution intend to view these or not or are you -- have you decided not to show these excerpts? When I say number 6, the transcripts can be found at tab number 6; 12, number 12; 15, number 15; 17, tab 17; 18, tab number 20; and 20, tab 20. What is to become of these videos?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, any tapes which we are not showing today or from this list, which we move on until tomorrow -- today and tomorrow, we withdraw. We will withdraw these tapes without prejudice. For example, tab number 6 in the binder, there's just a surrogate sheet mentioned. For some of these tapes it was not possible for the Prosecution to produce transcripts or translations. Other videos which are behind the tab numbers Your Honours have just mentioned, other videos contain footage of potential witnesses and the Prosecution does not intend to introduce such potential witness statements by way of a video in the current proceedings. For example, there is one video which plays after the events in Dusina. According to the information provided to me from our internal system, in there are a number of soldiers arriving at a -- not collection point, but at a point where a physician is present and they show their wounds. And while they show their wounds, they are talking about what they had just experienced, how they suffered these wounds. And this could be potential witness testimony, and for this reason such footage is currently withdrawn. Other sequences: We have one sequence which is playing at night. It shows burning houses. But since we cannot produce a witness at this late stage to identify exactly where he has taken the footage, where these houses are burning, the Prosecution made - at least for the time being - the call to withdraw them without prejudice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So the videos which I have mentioned, as well as the tabs you have just said that you're not going to show these for a number of reasons. So video number 6, because you don't have a transcript; and the other ones, because this could have been adduced by the witnesses. For instance, there is one video which shows houses which are burning in the night, but you are not able to establish which village is burning and what the date is. So you had rather withdraw these. 6, 12, 15, 17, 18, and 20 will therefore not be shown. And we have now before us this chart which you provided us at the beginning of the afternoon, and we shall now move on and continue showing these last videos. I shall give you the floor now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So the video V000-3764 will be played again with audio. It's transcript -- I provided the page -- the relevant page number earlier.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecutor please repeat the page where the transcript can be found.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The relevant transcript page is 28, starting with the second main paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And as Your Honours have suggested, we'll try to stop the tape at the moment when the person is raising the gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: THE NARRATOR: The mortar bomb landed close to them. May Allah have mercy upon them both. The Mujahedin leadership got together to establish the reasons for the defeats and the withdrawals. They found that the main reason was the lack of correct and sound Islamic beliefs amongst the members of the Bosnian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We'll make a second attempt to stop this tape I think in about half a second or one second, when the person is moving his head towards the camera.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has attempted to produce stills. However, the material from which we were working, which was not the original, did not allow us at this stage to produce a still in sufficient quality, so we will resort to this at a later stage. And the whole sequence from the beginning will be shown again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: THE NARRATOR: The mortar bomb landed close to them. May Allah have mercy upon them both. The Mujahedin leadership got together to establish the reasons for the defeats and the withdrawals. They found that the main reason was the lack of correct and sound Islamic beliefs amongst the members of the Bosnian army. In addition to this, there were traitors amongst the ranks of the army, a lack of good military planning and chaotic organisation during operations. The Shura Council for the Mujahedin decided to stop taking part with the army in any of the military operations until the Mujahedin were recognised as an independent battalion within the Bosnian army. The Bosnian army acknowledged the role that the Mujahedin had played so far and their need for men of this kind. Therefore, the Bosnian army leadership agreed to their request and recognised the Mujahedin Battalion as a part of the Bosnian army, over which the banner of [inaudible] could be raised. This gave them the ability to choose their soldiers based on the Islamic Sharia. Thus began a new stage in the war, with increasing responsibility and the need for planning and organisation. The head office for the battalion was in Zenica. The training camp was [inaudible] training camp in the village of Mehurici. The leader of the battalion was Abul-Harith, the Libyan, may Allah have mercy upon him. And the military commander was Wahiudeen, may Allah have mercy upon him. From this point, the Mujahedin launched their first operation, after the recognition of their battalion. This operation occurred in the summer of 1993, under the leadership of Wahiudeen, in the mountains surrounding the town of Vitez, which is inhabited by the Croats and is close to the town of Novi Travnik. A loss of [inaudible] enabled the Mujahedin to capture this area and they killed approximately 40 Croats.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So this video which lasts three minutes, begins by providing a commentary, which explains that the Mujahedin have got together for a number of reasons connected with the fact that there are traitors or the fact that they are disorganised. We see a Range Rover bearing a flag. We can assume that the flag is black but one cannot be 100 per cent sure of this. Then we see a Golf car with people inside. We also see a set where we see somebody shooting and a still image where one can identify the same as one could on a photograph. We also see these items which we mentioned in previous video viewings. And we can see the soldiers in a circle praying. And we see the banner of the Jihad, which we've seen already. We have the feeling that we have already seen such sequences in other video broadcasts. The only item we haven't seen before is a young person holding a machine-gun, and this young person is probably no more than 18 years old and he has a bandage on his head. He's wearing a bandanna on his head. It would be good to get a close-up of him. Also two other people, the doctor, Abul-Harith. His name is mentioned in the negotiation for the liberation of Turtic [phoen]. Haris and the Egyptian chief and the commentary which goes with it, and we can assume that they have both been killed. We see scenes of fighting and we can hear the words "Allahu Akbar" mentioned. We can see combatants that have been killed and which might be interesting. We can see a prisoner with his hands in his back. We don't know who the prisoner is but it seems quite clear that the prisoner has got his hands over his head. Although we see a date which is the 5th of September, we don't know at which it's the date at which the fight took place. We don't know, but we see this date here, the 5th of September. And during the commentary it is said that during the course of the combat 40 Croats have been killed. On this footage, we also see some rather characteristic white houses which would enable one to identify the location. So this is how one could view these three minutes of video footage. Defence counsel, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We shall refer to the comments we made on a former video which we have already seen concerning the Mujahedin, the video entitled "Martyrs in Bosnia." However, Your Honour, as regards this particular sequence, we have noted that several sequences have been collated and these various video sequences were probably shot at a different time. This is why this date of the 5th of September, 1993 might be applied to this particular video footage but we don't have the date of the other video footages. It seems clear that this has been collated, when we see the scene with the soldiers in a circle praying, when we look at the podiums, the podiums are empty, and then we see another scene where the podiums are full of people and people are sitting there. Tomorrow -- also, when we said that the comment has got nothing to do with the images that are shown here, the comment is really quite distinct from what one can see on these pictures. And lastly, Your Honour, there's one sequence which particularly drew our attention. It's the one where you can see -- or rather, where you can hear a shot probably fired from a mortar and you can see a houses that is burning. This may be a important scene, particularly if this video is being adduced into evidence, or this excerpt at any rate. And we don't even know if the combatants are Mujahedins or not in this particular excerpt. These could be Serbs fighting Croats. We wouldn't even know about it. Notwithstanding the fact the only clue provided here are the words "Allahu Akbar"; this is the only item which would enable us to identify the origin of these soldiers. For the foregoing reasons, we feel, Your Honours that, this scene no more than the others should be adduced into evidence. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. No further comments other than what Mr. Bourgon has already said. Our objections that we've raised already to these same sequences would apply equally to the ones we've just viewed. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Prosecution, you have the floor. If you would like now to show the video 5, 1468.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, would the Prosecution be permitted to make a brief statement, a brief commentary, at least to respond to the Defence's objections? Just briefly. We would just like to add two small details. The Prosecution observed on the tape also a religious leader which was present during the gathering who had a grey shirt or a grey religious coat and was wearing a kind of hat. This person appeared twice, once at the beginning and at the second time he was sitting nearly next -- or on the bench next -- three persons next to Wahiudeen. Wahiudeen, a person which we believe is Mr. Alagic, two other persons in uniform, and then this religious leader. Also, the Prosecution wishes to point out that there was mentioning about the head office of the battalion in Zenica. This can be found also in the transcript, on page 29 on the bottom. And there was some kind of gate or fence in front of this headquarter or alleged headquarter, and the Prosecution couldn't quite see the word which was on the fence. It looked like "Hrastova" [phoen]. But the Prosecution just wants to highlight this. Then there was also mentioning made of a training camp in the village of Mehurici. And these are in brief the additional observations of the Prosecution. And just two document which is have already been highlighted last week, PT91, contested exhibit 39 as well as PT92, contested exhibit 40, do show, in the Prosecution's opinion, that the incorporation occurred throughout the month of August, especially in the second document PT92, signed and stamped by Mr. Rasim Delic, the commander of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. It says under (iv) "Final provisions" under number 1 "Realisation of the task." What is meant is the incorporation of the unit, El Mujahedin: "Realisation of the task set by the present order is to begin immediately and to be finished not later than 31st August 1993." This, in the Prosecution's position, matches up with the date 5th September 1993, which is displayed in the -- at one of the footages shown on this tape, the first operation which was supposedly taking place on the 5th of September. Thank you, Your Honours. We will continue to show the next sequence. Or before, the Prosecution also likes to tender one still of this gathering into evidence. If I might ask the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you're asking that this still be admitted into evidence and it corresponds to what we saw at some point during the viewing; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. On the lower right-hand side, it says: "Still taken from V000-3764," which is the current tape. And then it give it is timecode, 1 hour, 17 minutes, 30 seconds. Just the issue of whether the banner contained the wording "Jihad" or "Brigada Jihad" was an issue last Friday, and for this reason the Prosecution has taken this still.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regarding the photograph that is being tendered, can we hear the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. First of all, this is an exhibit that does not figure on the Prosecution's list of documents, but we are not going to split hairs. This is a product from the video; therefore, Mr. President, we do object to its admissibility because we don't have a witness to tell us what it is about. This fully illustrates what the Defence has been saying, therefore: Who are these people? What is the flag? Who wrote the words? Who produced the video? There are so many questions. I have nothing more to say, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, in further observations. In our view the admissibility of the still would depend on the admissibility of the video. The two go hand in hand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are going to mark this document for identification because as you know we will have a final decision about these videos. So let us have an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P115, marked for identification, ID. 115 ID.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution also seeks to produce the other stills just suggested by your side a moment ago. And we will continue with the next footage, which is drawn from the tape V000-1468. It is a sequence of four minutes in duration, and it is from Radio TV Belgrade, RTB. It relates again to news and uses -- it's a juxtaposition. It uses excerpts from Sky TV and from BBC, which are shown on the four minutes on this news programme. The problem with the transcript or translation was that at some point in time on this tape there are two languages which can be heard simultaneously, B/C/S and the English original, because there is footage taken from such a company, Sky TV and BBC I just mentioned, and there is also a statement of Robert Fox, who is introduced as a member of the Daily Telegraph, which is a newspaper from the United Kingdom and Robert Fox is a journalist or was a journalist at this time. And also the reporter Jim Fish appears. The transcript can be found in tab 11; however, since the overwhelming majority of the excerpts shown today relate from the so-called reserve list, the Prosecution was only able to provide a kind of summary transcript or translation, and the excerpt is from 2 hours 38 minutes, and it says - I think it's the last page of this summary transcript or translation - It says around the footage 2 hours 40 minutes, 25 till 2 hours 42 minutes, "English transcription (translations.) The passage is not clear, since both the English original and the Serbo-Croatian translation could be heard simultaneously. Some mistakes might occur in this transcription." This just being said in advance. And the sequence will be played now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] ... is this morning on TV stations in the world. Humanitarian flights to Sarajevo will probably be renewed mid-week because an agreement has been signed on safe passage of planes. But in New York, the UN Security Council has voted a new resolution recommending that Yugoslavia be excluded from the United Nations. On the other hand, there are reports on the clear presence of Mujahedin in Bosnia, and at the peace conference in Geneva Muslim, Croat, and Serb leaders have signed an agreement on the protection of humanitarian flights and convoys using land routes. These flights will probably be renewed in mid-week. Passage of humanitarian flights is being ensured. Of course, it is expected that all three sides will abide by the agreement, and in the UN in New York the Security Council has decided to suspend Yugoslavia's right to vote in the General Assembly. However, the final decision should be taken by the General Assembly tomorrow. But this is a clear sign that the international community is angry. "There's a clear sign that we need to cover a long road before joining the international community. This is something that should be borne -- that they should bear in mind and ensure peace and respect the process that Mr. Vance and Owen have been working on so hard in Geneva." The leader of the Bosnian Serbs, Radovan Karadzic, took part in Geneva, where he described the war in Bosnia as a religious war, an armed conflict with the participation of a large number of people from the Islamic world fighting the Orthodox Serbs. "They're getting more and more weapon, not only from Germany but also from Islamic countries." Some evidence was found this week when the BBC prepared a story about the fighters in Travnik, who are allegedly from the Middle East. Reports speak of hundreds of Islamic volunteers or "Mujahedin" in this area. Some were secretly filmed, training the local Muslim forces. Observers are aware of their presence but claim that they're not involved in the conflict. "There are fighters that we don't know about, nor do we know their numbers. There may be many, maybe hundreds. They are providing a good armed support." The Islamic connection is further strained to keep the line between the Bosnian Croats and official forces composed mainly of Muslims. Croats fear what they call Islamic fundamentalism, and the others the territorial claims of the Croats. "From Iran to Europe there is support. They're using special flights to go to Croatia."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This video lasting four minutes, it appears to be the Novi Sad news bulletin by a speaker. We see a logo with a circle with the words "P/J." This tape refers to the presence of the Mujahedin. There is a compilation of various reports, including Sky News. We see excerpts from discussions in the Security Council - this appears to have taken place prior to the Vance-Owen Plan - and the British ambassador giving a statement is shown. We see a picture of Sarajevo, a building on fire, which apparently is the parliament building. Then there's a passage with a retirement home with an old lady, with someone younger next to her. Then there is a scene showing Karadzic, who speaks of a religious war, saying that the Mujahedin are provided with weapons from Germany and the Arab countries. Then there's a report on the fighters in Travnik, and we see very clearly well-dressed soldiers in military uniform, and according to the report it is in Travnik. Then again there is mention of Robert Fox and scenes of demonstrations. The term "Mujahedin" appears repeatedly during the story, and apparently this took place in Travnik. And the speaker says -- the announcer says that these images were obtained through secret sources, though we don't really know what those sources are. So one has the impression that we are seeing footage of these fighters, but as if taken from above, either by satellite or by planes secretly. It's very strange, because it appears to have been taken with infrared lights during the night. I may be wrong, but that is the impression one gets. I give the floor to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. For all the reasons already mentioned and mentioned by the Chamber, this is a document that has no credibility in spite of the reference to the word "Mujahedin." So this is evidence which would not assist the Chamber in any way to make a ruling regarding this trial. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's the same point that we've made time and time again, that there's nothing to verify that what is said by the commentator in fact matches what we see in the images. There's nothing which can tie the two together. In our view that means that the whole video, the commentary and the images, should not be admitted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Prosecution now, do you wish either to respond to what has been said or to introduce the next videotape, 2414, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution would continue. And the following tapes relate all to looting and destruction. Since these excerpts have been drawn from the reserve list, the Prosecution wants just to announce before these excerpts are being shown that they do not necessarily -- or not all of these excerpts go directly to crimes charged in the indictment. A few excerpts do, but other excerpts relate also to looting or destruction, instances which are in the area of the 3rd Corps or very close to the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps. And just to highlight this a little bit, the Prosecution has brought a rough map which was shown during the opening statement, just to give a kind of overview or to locate the footages which will be shown now. If I may ask the usher to put this on the ELMO. What can be seen: The coloured area is the area of the 3rd Corps, the area of responsibility with Zenica in the centre. The first footage relates to the destruction and looting of Croat villages in Kakanj, which lies to the east of Zenica. The excerpt is drawn from the tape V000-2414, and there is some information provided about the dates on these tapes, and they overwhelmingly come from July 1993 until November 1993. The tape is 42 minutes in its duration. It comes from the Defence counsels in the Blaskic case, and this tape was been handed over to the ICTY in the Blaskic trial as Defence Exhibit D531. The author of the tape is Pejo Orsolic from TV Kiseljak, and an indication of the date of the tape is given in the system. It is 24 June 1994. The sequence will be played now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. If I could just indicate that we did receive a copy of this CD. Unfortunately, we were not able to play it in our system. There appears to be a problem with the way in which it was burnt. But in our view, that's no reason to hold up proceedings. If the CD can be shown now and if time is needed at the end, we can request it, but it's unlikely that there will need to be a break. In our view, it's best that we just proceed with it now and then make comments after it has been shown. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] This was taped by brother Pejo Orsolic, a priest in Kraljeva Sutjeska parish, after the ethnic expulsion of Croats from the area of Kakanj municipality. We are in Borcici. This is the house of one of the Marjanovics. These are the results of Muslim vandalism. The Muslim woman who looted this, the goods and these things, managed to escape my camera, so I didn't get a chance to film her. The little that was left after looting committed by various formations is being looted by civilians. Everything is taken away. In the distance is the village of Lukici. You can see burnt houses there without roofs. This is Borcici again, a burnt house. Now we are on the other side of the village of Borcici; similar scenes. We didn't find any Croats among the inhabitants of the village of Borcici. We are passing through Brdo. This is the burnt house of Father Stjepan's sister. We are passing through Seoce. Among the few inhabitants left is this blind old woman. What is it? Don't cry all the time. I'm here. We are in Zajezda now. This is what remains after those who claim to be humane. Bjelavici; the interior of the parish church in Bjel. Here, have a look. During the last visit, the superior found communion wafers scattered and broken on the floor, which the MOS threw out of this sacred place. The glorious television of BiH won't say a word about this. In Bjelavici. This is the cultural level of a humane army: Excrement in the middle of the Catholic chapel in Bjelavici. A humane army. You've seen it well. This is the upper part to have village of Bjelavici. None of the inhabitants are here either. Nela, you've seen quite a lot of such things; right? Twenty days after the fighting ceased, the houses of Croats are still on fire. Where are these people supposed to return? To what? Our humane brothers, the Muslims, civilians, are plundering what remains and the helpless UNPROFOR members are just watching in disbelief. However Mr. Mujo, who is looting, will take it in his stride. And now some clips from Draganici. This is the house of Andrija Tunic. Animals were brought to these rooms on the floor. It seems that they were even slaughtered here, because there are some traces of blood. The room is full of excrement. Look at this. There are traces of blood. And there, look at the window-sill. Dung on the floor. And here on the wall there are traces of blood. Only the light is not good, so I cannot see that well. This here, however, can be seen clearly: Traces of blood. Whose house is this? It is Milos Marko and Ilija's and Marin's. There are three houses. This is the house of Marko Milos. What is this? The wardrobe is empty. This is the house of Simo Dujmovic. We are on the upper floor. Tresevo, in Bara. Come and see this. These are Stations of the Cross from the parish church in Bjelavici. The glass is mostly broken. This was brought in today. A picture of Saint Marko. Open this. This is the mass book from the chapel in Pavlovici. A chalice from Pavlovici. So ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a videotape lasting 42 minutes. There are scenes showing devastated houses and locations which are not part of the indictment, such as Bjelavici and Zajezda, and other locations that are not part of the indictment. Clearly the tape has been made either in the presence of Father Stjepan -- we see houses that were totally destroyed. This was clearly not done in a single day, because the damage in the interior of the houses is such that several individuals needed several days to do it. We also see burnt houses, even houses that are still burning. And according to the commentary this happened 20 days after the actual beginning of the looting. There are houses with smoke still coming out of them. There are several dates appearing on the film. I noted the 5th of July, the 6th of July, the 15th of July, the 25th of August, the 13th of November, the 15th of November, the 21st of November. And there is snow in the last images and it is the 20th of November, 1993. Then there's the church in Bjelavici, and we see the inside that has been damaged. We are shown a chalice, which is either broken or a hole made in it - we can't see too well - and a mass book. Towards the end of the video, we see people carrying away objects. Whether they are the owners of the buildings, of the houses. We don't know, but with the exception of one lady we only see young men carrying various objects with various means, carriages and cart wheels and -- but we don't see any soldiers at all. We only see civilians carrying all these things in a peaceful atmosphere. Everything is being done very calmly. And this occurred over several days, because we see the dates that appear and the person filming this is on an upper floor filming the people below carrying something and not knowing that they're being filmed. The video of the 20th of November is of a poor quality so we can't see exactly what is happening. There are houses whose owners are named - Simo Dujmovic, for instance - the 13th of July. Also at a certain point in time next to a scene of a looting, there is a blue helmet - we don't know who he is - but we clearly see a UN helmet and he is present, watching what is going on. What emerges from this is there isn't a single locations that is covered by the indictment. That is as much as can be said, in very concise form, but I'm not going to take 40 minutes to elaborate on what we've seen. Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. As the Chamber has seen, the tapes describing destruction and that seem to be describing looting also has no direct link with the indictment. And we are told that some parts of the videotape would be tied to the indictment, but we don't know which ones. At any rate, the names of villages we have heard are not part of the indictment, as the Trial Chamber has seen or heard. The Prosecution showed us a map to show us and indicate what the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps was. This was to describe a ROF [as interpreted], and I think that the Prosecution meant that this map provided an overall view without being too specific. This map, Your Honour, is full of mistakes. Let me just give you one example: There were three villages in Orasac. Which one is the one that figures in the indictment? We have no information as regards the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps. If as the Prosecution alleges this were to be relevant, we don't know what the area of responsibility is, we don't know what distance the front lines cover, we don't know which units are part of the 3rd Corps, we don't know how the 3rd Corps was organised, and we are involved in a trial where the responsibility of the command of the 3rd Corps is at stake. Several dates are mentioned here concerning these pictures we have seen. The beginning is in July 1993 and runs through to November. We don't know exactly which scene is shot at which particular time. We don't know in which town we are. There's a commentary here. We hear somebody giving the names of the towns. Usually when you want to shoot a scene in a village - I've seen other tapes prior to this - usually you film the signpost as you enter the village to give you an indication where you are. None of this appears here. And you would have to trust the person who is speaking without the person actually introducing himself or herself. The commentary, mentioned by Mr. Dixon earlier on. It seems that the comments were added on afterwards, after the pictures were taken, because we can clearly hear at certain stages the sound of this and the sound of the video being shot. Also, 20 days after the fighting, the houses are still burning. It's not because the houses started burning 20 days before that but it's because these houses started burning well after the fighting. We see civilians here. We see a Muslim woman who would have stolen the camera of the person who would have shot the video, Mr. Mujo, who is looting. We don't know anything about Mr. Mujo, who with his wheelbarrow seems to be transporting many objects. People are transporting things without us knowing whether these are looters or not. They are all civilians. There are no military people. We see scenes of looting. We don't know in which villages this looting takes place. For all these reasons, Your Honours, we feel that in the absence of any witness who could identify and authenticate these videotapes, these videotapes cannot be tendered, notwithstanding the fact, Your Honour, that we think that this videotape is totally irrelevant in this particular case.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
