utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Your Honours' summary and what Mr. Bourgon has said. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. It is now five minutes to 6.00. We shall resume -- it is twenty minutes to 6.00. We shall resume around 6.00. And if we are on time, we should finish with all the videotapes today. So we shall resume at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So the hearing is resumed. Let me turn to the Prosecution. From what I understood, the Prosecution was only going to show one video, number 10; is that correct? 2414, 10, a five-minute video footage. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the other excerpts from the tape V000-2414 are withdrawn without prejudice, and sequence number 11 has been shown on Thursday or Wednesday, I think Wednesday evening. And the only outstanding remaining sequence would therefore be 24 -- excuse me, yeah -- would therefore be 2414 from part 1, five minutes, with the timecode 1 hour 11 minutes and 10 seconds and then for five minutes. This sequence relates to the Croat population from Kakanj and Vares in November 1993, to be precise on the 4th of November, 1993. It will be played now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the interpreters have the page number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution cannot provide a page number here because the English translation produced does not contain a timecode. As far as the Prosecution is aware, there is not much to translate, so for this reason it is hopefully possible just to show the sequence. To be shown now.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] Croats expelled from the territory of Kakanj municipality to Vares.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So this five-minute video shows the Croats being driven out from Kakanj. You see hundreds of people, men, women, and children. There are not very many elderly people; some young children. You can see some youngsters who are laughing. One doesn't have the feeling that there is any kind of fear or that anybody is panic-stricken. I think these people seem to be waiting for something. Perhaps it's distribution of food or perhaps they're just waiting to move on and go elsewhere. We have no further piece of information. You see no policemen around and no soldier around. At one point you can see a car, which is -- seems to be bearing a white flag. It's a Red Cross perhaps car or flag. We don't know because the car is driving through quite fast, but you can see the flag. There are hundreds of people, perhaps 1.000 people milling around, but nobody seems to be worried by anything in particular. Nobody seems panic-stricken. There is no date here which would enable us to understand which time this gathering of people actually took place. That's as much as I can say as regards this five-minute videotape. The Defence team, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to Prosecution to specify something, please. Your Honours, this videotape is being provided in support of which part of the indictment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This videotape - I'm turning now to the Prosecution - which particular paragraph does it refer to? The perhaps that talks about Vares? And what is this videotape connected to? Which paragraph in the indictment, please? Which paragraph in the pre-trial brief, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, at the end of the first day there was another sequence of very short duration being shown which related to many people being moved to or from Vares, and this was the only additional piece of information which we could find from the video evidence which showed that civilians were being moved to or from Vares. I just recall a discussion relating to this one-minute videotape from TV5, and it was disputed, so to say that, population movements occurred, and this was the only additional video evidence which the Prosecution could identify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I'll give the floor back to the Defence team. I just omitted something. Some people might have been expelled from Kakanj to Vares. I would just like to say that I've seen nobody carrying suitcases or bags. When you leave some place, you usually take some belongings with you, particularly if you have children and young children with you, and you take some baby bottles or some food, and here it seems like nobody is carrying anything. That's as much as we can see. It seems like what we see here would have occurred before the 4th of November, the attack on Vares. So maybe this is dated the 2nd, the 3rd, or the 1st of November. We don't know. The Prosecution seems to establish a connection with Vares here, but without any further particulars.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. On reading the indictment, it is difficult to understand any connection between the videotape we've just seen and any allegation contained in the indictment. And for these reasons we believe, Your Honour, that what we have just seen is irrelevant and for this particular reason should not be tendered into evidence in the course of this particular trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Our position is exactly the same. It appears, also looking at the images, that the way the persons are dressed is not consistent with winter dress, which would be more in November time, and in our submission it's probably a time period much earlier than November. There's nothing on the videotape which indicates a time, although my learned friend from the Prosecution seemed to suggest that it was the 4th of November, that there's nothing in the tape or even the inscription on the bottom of the image which indicates a date. And in our view, there being no connection with the only part of the indictment relating to Vares in November, this evidence should be excluded. It's not relevant and it's not authenticated in any way. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I shall give the floor back to the Prosecution. The Defence alleges an interesting point, which is a valid one: The people shown on the video are dressed in summer clothes, and a few moments ago we saw videotape which was shot in the months of November and you could actually see the snow, and you could even see someone who was putting -- had put a number of things on a sledge, whereas this place was not very far removed from the other one we saw. There might be perhaps a maximum of 50 or 100 kilometres between these villages. Does the Prosecution wish to talk about this and talk about the dates and the locations indicated here, and on the weather conditions on the 4th of November or a few days prior to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have no further comment to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Thank you. We have concluded the viewing of all the videotapes which the Prosecution on request of the Trial Chamber has decided to show. There has been a discussion or debate between the two parties. The Defence team has submitted its arguments; the Prosecution has been entitled to take the floor again. We've had an adversarial debate and the Trial Chamber will render a decision on the tendering into evidence of these videotapes. As far as things stand today, we can conclude that we have finished viewing these videotapes and the tendering into evidence of these videotapes. As I have said, we shall render a decision on this as soon as we have more information about them. What I mean by this are the archivists and the witness who is a high-ranking military who may provide further details as concern this particular issue. That said, the next hearing will be on Wednesday, and we will have this hearing in order to address these other issues, the question relating to the archivists. Unless the Prosecution, as we still have 40 minutes left, can tell us more about the archivists and may be able to say that there's no point in convening on Wednesday. If we meet again on Wednesday, I'll be delighted to see you all, of course, but we will then hold a rather short hearing, because one of the Judges is involved in another case. In that case, we will have our hearing between 9.00 and 10.00 in the morning. Unless you have other things to raise or other issues to raise, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. At this point the Prosecution would certainly be happy to appear Wednesday morning at 9.00, but perhaps a better course of action or one which would be quicker would simply be for us to inform the Chamber and the Defence in writing with respect to the availability of the witnesses for the week commencing the 21st of June. As I indicated earlier, we anticipate that we will have a full slate of witnesses for that week, but I'm not in a position to confirm the precise order of those witnesses until I've had the opportunity to discuss the matter with Ms. Benjamin. Assuming that she is in the office tomorrow, we will be in a position to disclose to the Defence the additional witness statements which were taken. We will be in a position to confirm with the witnesses the precise dates for their appearance here, and we can certainly inform the Chamber and the Defence pursuant to the letter and the same format that has been used throughout the Prosecution case. I don't anticipate having any other issues that would necessitate us being on the record with respect to those witnesses, but we could certainly inform everyone in writing as to the precise order. In accordance with the practice that Ms. Benjamin and I employ, she did ask the witnesses of their availability in the week of the 21st of June and all of the witnesses are available in that time period. It's simply a question of which one will go on Monday, Tuesday, et cetera. So once she's in, I expect it would just be a relatively quick process to disclose the witness statements to the Defence, to contact the witnesses, schedule them in, and provide in writing a formal notification letter, perhaps by Wednesday, assuming, again, she's in tomorrow. And that, in our submission, would thereby render it not necessary for us to sit on Wednesday. I do have one other issue relating to this matter: In light of the fact that we have been ordered by the Trial Chamber to bring the archivists here, it might be helpful for some guidance, in terms of whether with respect to those witnesses that we've been ordered to produce, whether the Trial Chamber would also like copies of the witness statements that we've taken. I know that earlier we did provide statements and then we stopped that practice. The Defence may, of course, like to be heard on that point. We are certainly willing to provide any statements taken to the Chamber, if that would be helpful. And I do have one other unrelated issue, but if you'd like to hear from the Defence on the issue of witness statements, we could do that now or I could raise the final issue that I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I shall give the floor to the Defence team. As far as the archivists are concerned - and the Trial Chamber has conferred over this - of course we are very keen to have any written statements which these people may have made. So if you give us these, we will read them very happily before the hearing. The Prosecution may, of course, ask questions to these archivists. We will then have a cross-examination. And the Judges - and I feel that the question that a Judge may have as regards these archivists is, A, how did they take possession of these archives, at what date; how did -- were these archives communicated to them; how were these archives recorded at the time these archives were produced; were the contents of these archives broadcast to the outside world; who accessed the contents of these archives; and according to what you have said, why were there some 7th Brigade archives located in another area and the BiH archives were not in the same place? So these will be questions of a purely theoretical nature. We will not address this issue in substance, because they will be asked how they actually got hold of these documents, how they were recorded, and who could access these documents. I'm sure you yourselves will put these questions to them, and the Judges may in that case not ask them anything specific. But insofar as these people have made written statements, I'm sure they have covered all of this ground. So I'm sure the Defence team has something to say about the archivists.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. No additional observations to make in addition to those made by the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the other Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. The statements, as has been suggested by the Prosecution, should be given, in our view, to Your Honours. I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. There's general consensus regarding these statements and them being provided to the Defence counsel, of course, in the first place. Your other issue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And I will ensure that copies of those statements are provided at the time we inform the Chamber and the Defence as to the precise order. Mr. President, the second issue concerns the documents that were provided pursuant to the Chamber's order concerning the known original signatures of the two accused. During previous discussions with the Chamber's legal officer on this issue, I am now led to believe that there may have been some confusion. We did make available, as Your Honours are aware, two types of documents with respect to both of the accused. The Rule 68/Rule 70 receipts were documents that were retained by the Office of the Prosecutor. Those original signatures came from a receipt binder that Mr. Withopf took care of and which I now have possession of. The arrest packages, however, Mr. President, were entered into the Evidence Unit and there is, accordingly, chain-of-custody documents associated with those folders. This is where I believe the confusion came in. I'm not sure when I discussed this issue with the legal officer if she fully understood that those were actually evidence, which is why they have ERN numbers. And I simply raise this point, Mr. President, because it may be problematic to have originals taken from the Evidence Unit and tendered into evidence. I am fully aware of the need for the originals to be retained, but it is a bit of a problem at this point, particularly with respect to those arrest packages, the turquoise-blue folders, simply because they have been signed out by an investigator from the Evidence Unit and there was an expectation that those would be returned to the Office of the Prosecutor, to be returned to the Evidence Unit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you give me the two packages with the Kubura and Hadzihasanovic signatures that we gave you last time. Last time you gave us in two folders several documents. And last night, in fact, I asked myself regarding the arrest warrants that were signed by the accused. According to the Rules, the arrest warrant is executed by the Registrar. When the Confirming Judge confirms the indictment and signs the arrest warrant, which I did some time ago. The arrest warrant is given to the Registrar, who is depository of it. And the Registrar, according to the Rule, makes certified copies, which are authenticated, and these copies are then given to the States for the execution of arrest warrants. Therefore, the Prosecution may have a copy, but the original is kept by the Registrar. If the Prosecution does have a certified copy, let us take the hypothesis that the accused is arrested and he is notified of the arrest warrant. I have one here in front of me. Normally this arrest warrant, in my understanding, should be returned to the Registrar. I don't understand why the Prosecution should keep an act, a document, which is an integral part of the procedure, because the arrest warrant goes together with the indictment and theoretically, when the formalities regarding notification of arrest warrant have been completed, it should be returned to the Registrar. And in fact, last week I wondered, I asked myself, how is it possible that the Prosecution should have this document in its possession? In theory, after the notification, the Prosecution should send the original back to the Registrar and keep a copy for itself. But you kept the original. And you are telling us now that it should be returned to you. This does not seem to me to be at all in line with the spirit and letter of the Rules, which says that it is the Registrar who executes the arrest warrant and when the persons -- a suspect is arrested, the arrest warrant should be returned to the Registrar. However, amongst the documents that you gave us there are some that have nothing to do with the arrest warrant, and of course in that case, it is normal that you should keep them. So, Mr. Mundis, regarding the question of the arrest warrant, could you enlighten the Chamber regarding the fact that you have in your possession the original of the arrest warrant, or -- if you can, of course, answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will add that to the list of other information that I need to provide to the Trial Chamber. I'm certainly in no position to answer the question as to how that document or sets of those two folders of documents came into the possession of the Prosecution, nor am I familiar with the actual process of how individuals are either arrested or surrendered to the custody of the Tribunal, what happens to those original documents, whether the copies that were in our Evidence Unit, perhaps, were certified original copies that were retained. I simply am not in a position to articulate that. But I will certainly make the requisite inquiries and inform the Trial Chamber and the parties as soon as I'm able to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Apart from this question of arrest warrant, it would be desirable, as everything has been recorded, that you keep in touch with the registrar and indicate which are the documents that you feel should be returned to you, because there's the arrest warrant, which in my opinion should be kept by the registrar, and then there are other documents that we have taken. But what mattered for us was the signature, and that is quite sufficient for us. So see with the registrar and then orally next week you can tell us which are the documents that you wish to regain possession of. But also, we would like you to let us know how it is that you have the original of the arrest warrant, whereas it would be normal for the Registrar to keep the original and to be the depository of the same. Thank you, Mr. Mundis. If our understanding is correct, you will be sending us a schedule for the hearings from the 21st and in that schedule you will indicate the witnesses that you have contacted through Ms. Benjamin and other witnesses too who will appear as of the 21st. And in view of that, there's no need for us to meet again on Wednesday. Also, the Chamber would like to raise another issue, but to do that let us go into private session, Mr. Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 14th day of June, 2004, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.55 p.m.,
